subject.title: Provider key pools + bucket-aware cooldown/backoff on 429 (Gemini projects) to prevent retry storms

question: Should OpenClaw add a native provider-pool/bucket contract for Gemini project-scoped key rotation, or should this remain an external sidecar/plugin pattern until the broader provider-profile routing design is settled?
rationale: The remaining gap is real, but implementing it touches auth/profile routing, config/defaults, persisted cooldown state, docs, and provider ownership boundaries that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design native bucket-aware provider pools
options.body: Keep this issue open and define bucket metadata, cooldown scope, doctor/docs behavior, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Make the broader routing issue canonical
options.body: Move the remaining work under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41135 if maintainers want one provider-pool routing design to own API keys, OAuth profiles, concurrency, and quota buckets.

options.title: Keep it external for now
options.body: Document current flat key rotation and let sidecars or plugins manage project buckets until a missing core extension API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design native bucket-aware provider pools
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define bucket metadata, cooldown scope, doctor/docs behavior, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the current generic API-key rotation surface and is the strongest single history signal for the provider/auth routing decision.
